title: Map Unit Converter: Scales, Ratios and Ground
description: Convert between map units with the Map Unit Converter — scale ratios, ground distances, inches and centimetres on the map. Free.
summary_sentence: For example, at 1:50,000 one centimetre is 500 metres of ground and one inch is about 0.79 miles — the two sentences every paper-map reader eventually memorises, converted here for any scale.

faq: What does this tool convert?
Among scale ratio, map distance (cm/in) and ground distance (m/km/mi) — any one to the others, by the representative-fraction relation.
Do I need an account?
No — values in, conversions out.
Can I use the result for professional work?
The arithmetic is exact; professional care goes to the source scale's truth (prints shrink, scans stretch — verify against the scale bar).
Which datum do these coordinate tools use?
WGS84 — tile systems are defined over it.
Do more decimal places always mean better accuracy?
No — tiles and pixels quantise; decimals beyond the cell are decoration.
Verbal scales ('one inch to four miles')?
Convert to a ratio first (4 miles = 253,440 inches → 1:253,440) — the converter accepts the ratio form, and the verbal form becomes it in one multiplication.
Bar scales?
A drawn bar survives photocopy scaling — measure the bar, derive the effective ratio, then convert with confidence.
Screen maps have scales?
Only relative to a physical screen size — which is why digital mapping switched to metres-per-pixel and zoom. Both worlds are served on this site.
Area scales?
Areas scale by the ratio squared — 1 cm² at 1:50,000 is 0.25 km². Square the linear factor, always.
Odd denominators?
Any ratio converts — historical sheets use delightful ones (1:10,560, six inches to the mile, among them).
